I am a Head and Neck Surgeon in Ottawa and I see patients at three sites : Carleton Place Hospital ; I rent a room at a hearing aid clinic ( in which I see everything from stuffy noses to ear infections to hearing loss ) ; and at a private practice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Carleton Place Hospital , like The Ottawa Hospital , has been providing frequent and excellent updates as to the functioning of the hospital , as well as guidelines for managing the COVID-19 pandemic . The public should be assured that the hospitals are being proactive and making excellent decisions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What is concerning is that initially , there was limited to no direction for those of us who run and manage out-of-hospital facilities . Thus far , those recommendations we did receive are somewhat confusing and contradictory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On March 17 , the Ontario Medical Association offered guidance on elective surgery ( non-emergency ) and non-essential medical visits . I am a surgeon here in Ottawa , so this was of interest . The OMA advice was to postpone routine and non-urgent assessments ( e.g. annual assessment screening programs and non-urgent , elective consults , and elective surgeries ) . This prompted the cancellation of all surgery at Carleton Place Hospital . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The &lt;a href= " https : //www.cpso.on.ca/ " &gt;College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario&lt;/a&gt; , which is responsible for licensing and monitoring physicians , indicated that during a &amp;ldquo ; Public Health Emergency&amp;rdquo ; physicians must be available to provide physician services such as providing direct medical care to people in need . When deciding what role to take during public health emergencies , physicians must do so in accordance with the values , principles and duties of medical professionalism. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All physicians in my situation understand that our role is to continue to care for patients in the best way we can , while at the same time not harming patients or putting them at risk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My medical practice at the hearing aid centre , for the most part , only assesses non-urgent patients . The problem is , I have one examination chair in which all patients will sit . Half of my patients are elderly and/or with medical co-morbidities ( transplants , asthma , heart disease , etc ) . Although many are young and healthy , I see between 30 and 45 patients a day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Due to being a small clinic , we do not have enough Personal Protective Equipment ( PPE , gowns , gloves , masks ) to protect ourselves and our patients with a high volume in clinical outpatient care outside the hospital in this current environment . Furthermore , we do not have isolation rooms , nor are we prepared to isolate a patient . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We have received some advice from the Canadian Medical Protective Agency ( CMPA ) with respect to some of our responsibilities when we do not have the ability to protect ourselves and patients with PPE . The CMPA indicated that if we do not practise due to not having personal protective equipment , we put ourselves at risk in terms of medical liability and investigations by the CPSO . I certainly hope in these circumstances , the CPSO and patients understand the difficulty in situations like ours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My private clinic is a bit simpler as it is non-essential services . However , there are significant economic impacts for all private medical clinics . Like most out-of-hospital physician offices , we have staff who work in our clinic . This includes nurses , administrators and other health care providers . If the doctors don&amp;rsquo ; t work , the clinic can not create income for the clinic and this puts jobs at risk . This is the case in all industries right now ; medical clinics are no different . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , right now we need to think bigger . This is a public health issue . We have been diligent with respect to screening , cleaning and ensuring patients are safe . It is a low risk environment at most times . However , recent studies on COVID-19 indicate that a large proportion of COVID-positive patients may be asymptomatic carriers who can spread the disease . Nevertheless , some important decisions need to be made in the short term to ensure we do our part to protect everyone . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Personally , I am taking proactive steps and I hope my decisions are the right ones . My biggest worry is my elderly patients and those with comorbidities . Do I cancel all patients and thus , new patients who have been waiting six to nine months wait longer ? Do I only cancel older patients or those with a co-morbidity ? Do I screen patients and hope that no asymptomatic carriers enter the clinic ? Am I helping or hurting with either decision ? Do I see fewer patients ? Do I cancel all my patients or do I work as scheduled ? Right now , I am using my own personal judgment and knowledge of population health to guide me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Initially , we planned on seeing patients in our clinic . However new evidence of asymptomatic COVID-19 spreading , referred to as &amp;ldquo ; stealth spreading , &amp;rdquo ; as well as recommendations from the government of Canada altered our view . Maintaining social distancing prevents spread but in a medical practice , there is only so much we can do to maintain distance . We can limit the number of patients in the waiting room , see fewer patients and screen diligently . Even with this , risks remain and I question if in-person clinic visits are safe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the end , I decided to adopt a tele-health model by calling new patients and conducting the medical assessment over the phone . The OMA and the Ontario Ministry of Health have been exceptionally helpful in arranging this for all physicians . This is my first time using this model of health care and I still have concerns , but it is the best option for me right now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The biggest problem is patient safety without a comprehensive physician examination . How can I look in someone&amp;rsquo ; s mouth/ears or nose from a phone ? I can&amp;rsquo ; t , so I may miss something . It is stressful as a physician trying to decide what is the best method to ensure this doesn&amp;rsquo ; t happen . We do have the option of e-mail and Skype consults , but with that come more concerns , primarily confidentiality . There is always a risk of hacking , email errors and putting patients&amp;rsquo ; confidentiality at risk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the end , I am going to do what I can . I just finished my first morning of tele-health-based ENT &amp;ndash ; Head and Neck Surgery clinic . All patients were very happy they received a phone call and all were understanding of the difficulty we face . I will continue to help as many as I can and prevent putting people at risk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , medical societies , Health Canada and public health should provide specific guidelines and advice for my clinic and similar medical clinics ( such as walk-in clinics ) . With the focus on hospitals , rightfully so , it is important for the public and those advising hospitals to understand the role we have in the current environment . Community and emergency physicians are the first line of care in our system . When functioning well , we help ease the strain on the system and prevent overcrowding in emergency departments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **26;12638;TOOLONG . James P. " data-portal-copyright= " CHRISTINNE MUSCHI " **28;13247;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1583954 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Wednesday , Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and President Donald Trump announced that Canada and the U.S. will jointly close the border to all non-essential traffic due to the COVID-19 pandemic . When the policy takes effect , cross-border shoppers and tourists will be turned away , as border crossings are restricted to essential workers , truckers and others who facilitate trade between the two countries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Closing Canada&amp;rsquo ; s border with the U.S. is something the provinces have been asking for since Monday , when Canada announced that Americans would be exempt from a new policy to restrict entry by foreign nationals to slow the spread of COVID-19 . Removing the American exemption was particularly important to British Columbia , a province struggling to contain the outbreak locally amidst unwelcome tourist visits by Americans wanting to take advantage of our weakened dollar . In addition , the U.S.&amp;rsquo ; s deep mishandling of the pandemic &amp;ndash ; from inadequate testing to defiant millennials partying at bars to the large number of Canadian cases attributable to travel to the U.S. &amp;ndash ; has made Canadians realize that our shared border currently poses a major public health threat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since Monday&amp;rsquo ; s announcement to close Canada&amp;rsquo ; s borders to other foreign nationals , hints were offered in press conferences that Canadian and American officials were discussing closing our shared border as well . Thus , Wednesday&amp;rsquo ; s announcement was not a major surprise , and represents an important step to reduce the transmission of cases into Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , Canadian officials were right to pursue a joint decision with the Americans to ensure bilateral trade and commerce continue . On a normal day , $2.4 billion in goods and services cross the border , and trade with the U.S. supports two million Canadian jobs . In these incredibly destabilizing times , it&amp;rsquo ; s imperative that some economic activity continues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition , some of the goods coming into Canada from the U.S. will be medical equipment and supplies needed to address the pandemic , while other shipments will fill Canada&amp;rsquo ; s grocery store shelves with fresh fruits and vegetables . Canadian officials also would have been seeking to work closely with the unpredictable Trump administration to ensure the restrictions are time-limited and implemented in good faith on both sides of the border . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet , despite the carefully crafted assurances by both leaders that bilateral trade will not be affected , we know &lt;a href= " https : **33;13277;TOOLONG ... the research evidence&lt;/a&gt; on Canada&amp;rsquo ; s past experience that this is false . Canadian trade with the U.S. will certainly be negatively impacted by these border restrictions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nearly two decades ago , the U.S. closed its border to Canada entirely following the 9/11 attacks . Perishable food spoiled as trucks waited days to cross . In the months following the border&amp;rsquo ; s reopening , heightened security procedures led to long line-ups and some cross-border supply chains dissolved as U.S. companies replaced their Canadian inputs with American substitutes . Passenger vehicles crossings for shopping and tourism were cut in half . As the more dependent trade partner , Canadian interests were hurt much more than American ones . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;13312;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;13354;TOOLONG ... Large companies with integrated supply chains invested heavily in border facilitation efforts , as did provinces such as Ontario that rely on the auto sector . Trusted traveller programs such as NEXUS and FAST were established . The Beyond the Border initiative was launched jointly by President Barack Obama and Prime Minister Stephen Harper to focus officials on facilitating better , faster two-way trade . We learned that it takes daily effort at many levels to maintain open trade across our border . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The threat posed by COVID-19 has made this extreme measure necessary . But as Canada and the U.S. implement the new policy , border guards and travellers alike will be confused about who is an essential worker and what kind of crossings are allowed . In addition , COVID-19 health protocols will still need to be followed to avoid undermining the policy&amp;rsquo ; s purpose . All of these rules must be worked out quickly and clear guidance offered to everyone affected . He had a voluminous scarf tied around his neck in that inimitable French fashion , a vintage tweed coat and a beaten-up leather satchel . Snapping down the kickstand of his rusty old bike , he glided from table to table greeting his comrades with &amp;ldquo ; la bise. &amp;rdquo ; Every cheek was proffered . Every cheek was kissed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Nantais are proud of their heritage and the urban environment plays a daily role in their schools&amp;rsquo ; curricula . In the city&amp;rsquo ; s formal park , the Jardin des Plantes , the Mus&amp;eacute ; e d&amp;rsquo ; Arts de Nantes , and the medieval castle that occupies the centre of town , the brooding Ch&amp;acirc ; teau des ducs de Bretagne , I saw gaggles of happy children and sloping adolescents follow along behind harried teachers . Tourists and residents intermingled with les &amp;eacute ; l&amp;egrave ; ves , who blocked entry ways , filled lobbies and streamed past couples on benches and afternoon walkers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On March 12 , President Macron announced the closure of all schools and universities but the city&amp;rsquo ; s boulangeries and p&amp;acirc ; tisseries continued to do brisk business . Sometimes the croissants , pains au raisins and tartes aux fruits are partially protected by acrylic screens . Sometimes not . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Baguettes are sold with a thin piece of paper wrapped around the loaf&amp;rsquo ; s centre and carried home uncovered . I watched young parents hold a baguette in one hand and a child&amp;rsquo ; s hand in the other . I saw baguettes tossed into the bottom of strollers , slipped into the corner of backpacks and carried underarm through crowded streets . I saw a dad tear off a chunk of baguette for his child to eat as she danced around a crowded store . I saw no evidence of hand sanitizer. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On March 14 , French Prime Minister &amp;Eacute ; douard Philippe announced the closure of &amp;ldquo ; all places that are not essential for the life of the country , &amp;rdquo ; including stores , caf&amp;eacute ; s , restaurants and cinemas . Now a debate rages in the media about whether the government&amp;rsquo ; s rapidly changing response will be enough to curb the spread of the coronavirus or whether the country is heading towards the same situation as Italy . From what I have observed of the daily habits of this proud people , I am not optimistic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before President Macron imposed the near total lockdown on human movement on March 16 and a friend was fined by police for jogging , the only person I saw exhibit awareness of the pandemic in Nantes was a shopper at the check-out of my local Monoprix supermarket , where aisles were busy and shelves reassuringly well-stocked . Remembering one last thing , she darted away and returned smiling , waving a few sleeves of disinfectant wet wipes . Ah , I thought . She&amp;rsquo ; s preparing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She bagged her groceries , pocketed her change , picked up with her bare hand the uncovered baguette that lay on the conveyer , and walked towards the door . Outside , darkness had fallen . A crowded street and a troubling future awaited . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **26;14435;TOOLONG . Ontario doesn&amp;rsquo ; t currently have sufficient hospital beds to deal with this emergency . I suggest the provincial government , with backing from federal emergency powers , requisition hotels to serve as temporary hospitals for the duration of the pandemic . Payments can be made to the hotels . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This would be a win-win situation for both the medical community and the hospitality industry , which&amp;nbsp ; is facing a drastic reduction in business . The disruption of global supply chains ; the near-total shutdown of international travel as Europe&amp;rsquo ; s airports are closing and the daily stream of nearly 200,000 people crossing the Canada-U.S. border dwindling to a trickle ; and the radical contraction of the world&amp;rsquo ; s primary economies . All bolts from the blue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sept. 11 , 2001 was similarly one of those events that &amp;ldquo ; crash down on our heads from a blue sky , &amp;rdquo ; and 10 years later , beginning in Tunisia in January , 2011 , the Arab Spring took everyone equally by surprise , in the same way that the uprisings in Poland and Hungary did in 1989 , when the Berlin Wall was pulled down , and the world was changed utterly . You&amp;rsquo ; d probably have to reach back to the War Measures restrictions of the 1940s to find the closest comparison with the draconian measures adopted across Europe and North America to contain the rising pace and spreading scale of the COVID-19 sickness that has suddenly afflicted more than 200,000 people worldwide , killing more than 8,000. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Where this is all going , and what sort of world we&amp;rsquo ; ll soon be living in , is still very much up to the people of the world&amp;rsquo ; s liberal democracies to decide , or at least to influence . " data-portal-copyright= " JOHN THYS " **28;15991;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1583204 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;16021;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;The Citizen has asked a group of medical and research experts to answer reader questions about COVID-19 . Here 's today 's query ( and we 'll try to answer others as we receive them ) : &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Question : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;strong&gt;I see a lots of people wearing masks but we 're told that 's not needed if you 're not ill . However , some people are also wearing gloves . Is that actually helpful in preventing the spread of COVID-19 ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **35;16057;TOOLONG &lt;strong&gt; ( courtesy of Dr. Adam Kassam , Chair , Section of PM&amp;R ( Physiatry ) , Ontario Medical Association ) : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Medical gloves , while helpful for health care personnel , shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be worn by the general public . Not only does this potentially generate a false sense of security for those wearing them , gloves might not actually help prevent the spread of COVID-19. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s because individuals wearing gloves might touch other objects as well as parts of their face &amp;ndash ; including their eyes , nose and mouth &amp;ndash ; which would have the same consequences for viral spread as if they had not worn gloves . Importantly , those wearing gloves also have to change them frequently in order to maintain proper precautions , which significantly diminishes the needed supply for health care workers on the front lines , who are on the brink of shortages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gloves are also not that durable ; they often rip , which reduces their effectiveness . They are not meant for daily activities and therefore should not be worn outside a health care setting . Finally , wearing gloves may provide another surface for the virus to live on &amp;ndash ; potentially encouraging transmission if not disposed of correctly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The best thing we can do is continue to focus on diligent hand hygiene : frequently washing with soap and water for 20 seconds ; avoid touching our face ; coughing/sneezing into our elbows ; and avoiding handshakes. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;16094;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;16136;TOOLONG ... Your questions answeredhttp : **32;17295;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;17329;TOOLONG ... title= " Keep washing and sanitizing those hands ! " alt= " Keep washing and sanitizing those hands ! " data-portal-copyright= " LIONEL BONAVENTURE " **28;17365;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1578625 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;17395;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;The Citizen has asked a group of medical and research experts to answer reader questions about COVID-19 . Here 's today 's query ( and we 'll try to answer others as we receive them ) : &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Question : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If I catch COVID-19 and recover , am I then resistant and safe from getting it again ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Answer , courtesy of Earl G. Brown , Emeritus Professor of Virology , University of Ottawa : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The question specifically asks whether what is formally called the SARS CoV 2 virus , which causes the COVID-19 disease , can re-infect humans after they have recovered from infection . Experiments that address this have not been performed and so the formal answer is : Unknown . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the biology of the SARS CoV 2 and the nature of human infections with other coronaviruses strongly suggest that you can not be re-infected with the same virus &amp;ndash ; at least not immediately after infection . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here&amp;rsquo ; s the reasoning : It is known that SARS CoV 2 respiratory infection proceeds to disease symptoms after two to 14 days . The virus test , which identifies virus genetic material ( RNA ) in nasal secretions by using a quantitative RT-PCR reaction , can detect virus beginning before symptoms and until the virus is cleared by the body after recovery . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The immune system is able to destroy 100 per cent of the virus produced during the infection and any re-infection at this time would be faced with a fully protective immune response . Human infections with other respiratory coronaviruses appear on a two-year cycle so it seems that immunity is not permanent but does protects for a year or two after infection . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are reports of COVID-19 patients who test positive one day and negative the next , especially early in infection ; this is due to the reduced sensitivity of the test to detect low levels of virus early in infection . So , it is possible that some patients appear to go from virus positive to negative before becoming positive again in later days as a consequence of a single incidence of infection ; not re-infection. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;17431;TOOLONG ... grocery shopping hours springing up at Independent Grocers , Shoppers Drugs&lt;/a&gt; &lt;strong&gt; &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;17466;TOOLONG ... closes Tweed visitor centre in Smiths Falls , switching to e-commerce&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;17501;TOOLONG ... the coronavirus , from Wuhan , China to Canada 's capital : A COVID-19 timeline&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;17536;TOOLONG ... BrownTue , 17 Mar 2020 18:21:11 **45;17571;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildHealthDenley : What 's more damaging , COVID-19 or the panic over it ? http : **37;17618;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;17657;TOOLONG ... title= " An aerial view from a drone shows an area of Miami Beach that the city closed in an effort to prevent the spread of the coronavirus. " data-portal-copyright= " Joe Raedle " **28;17693;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1581983 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is always a stark contrast between Florida and Ottawa in March , but never more than now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last weekend , I made a homeward-bound stop in the charming northern Florida town of Fernandina Beach , which seemed to have declared a COVID-19 awareness-free-zone . Bars and restaurants were packed , people browsed in shops and there wasn&amp;rsquo ; t a hint of the worldwide virus panic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One restaurant provided a mixture of oil and sea salt in the bathroom , so everyone could dip their fingers into it for some all-important exfoliation . When my wife suggested that perhaps that wasn&amp;rsquo ; t too smart , given the virus situation , an employee said they were thinking about taking it out , the next day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Arriving back in Ottawa , we found a city that is largely shut down , the virus the dominant fact of local life . It is difficult to gauge the level of fear here , but our leaders are doing all they can to stoke it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Are Floridians under-reacting or are we over-reacting , and what is the rational path ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At this point , the panic has had far greater impact than the disease itself . The Canadian economy is going into recession , people&amp;rsquo ; s jobs are threatened and their life savings have been drastically reduced by the stock market collapse , all over an infection that had , as of Tuesday morning , about 440 cases and four deaths . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To put that in context , there have been more than 35,000 cases of the normal , boring influenza A and influenza B in Canada so far this flu season , according to Infection Prevention and Control Canada . Each year , between 500 and 1,500 people die from these types of influenza , yet most Canadians can&amp;rsquo ; t even be bothered to get a flu shot . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Flu of any type can be serious for the elderly and those with compromised immune systems , but for all others the chance of dying from the new COVID-19 is remarkably low . And yet , most governments are reacting as if it were the bubonic plague . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Their policy approach is well-intentioned . No one wants see people die of disease and people have been conditioned to expect that when there is a problem , government must have a solution . That belief will be sorely tested by COVID-19. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Governments&amp;rsquo ; main tool is to shut down all non-essential activity for two weeks in the hope that the rate of increase in new cases will flatten out or even decline . It might well do , but then what ? We can&amp;rsquo ; t ask people to stay home indefinitely , and it&amp;rsquo ; s not realistic to expect that we can turn our country into a virus-free environment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada has closed its borders , with the rather large exception of allowing in up to 330 million Americans . Some have wondered why we didn&amp;rsquo ; t bar them , too . The simple answer is that we can&amp;rsquo ; t , if we still hope to have food and an economy . That leaves us vulnerable to America&amp;rsquo ; s patchwork response to COVID-19 , but it&amp;rsquo ; s unavoidable . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sure , we can ask Canadians to self-isolate for 14 days when returning from the U.S. , but what&amp;rsquo ; s the point ? Infection rates are no higher there than they are here and Americans flow into Canada every day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The most pressing reason to attempt to control the infection rate is the shocking , but not surprising , state of Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s health care system . Americans have expressed some concern because their hospital occupancy rate is 65 per cent . In Ottawa , we are routinely at full capacity and beyond . &amp;nbsp ; If there is one problem governments need to fix , this is it . We are poorly positioned to handle any big disease outbreak . COVID-19 ought to be a wake-up call on that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sometime soon , Canadians and their governments will need to step back and ask if our attempts to contain COVID-19 are effective or sustainable . The answer is unlikely to be encouraging . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **31;17723;TOOLONG Denley&lt;/strong&gt; is an Ottawa political commentator and author . COVID-19 -- How far can we go with closing the border ? http : **33;17945;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;17980;TOOLONG ... title= " The arrivals area at Trudeau Airport in Montreal on Monday . " data-portal-copyright= " Ryan Remiorz " **28;18016;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1581743 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The COVID-19 situation is rapidly evolving and governments are having a hard time keeping up with strategies to keep their citizenry safe . Some countries appeared to dismiss the seriousness of the virus for far too long ( hello , Trump administration ) , while others imposed what some felt were draconian measures ( China , Singapore ) that would not fly in a Western liberal democracy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of those measures was the closure of borders to prevent alleged &amp;ldquo ; disease carriers&amp;rdquo ; from entering one&amp;rsquo ; s land and spreading the infection . In one sense this was the right response as the virus did originate in a part of China late last year and an immediate ban on travel would have prevented any further dissemination . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The time to do that has long passed , however , as COVID-19 is already present in most countries &lt;del&gt; -- &lt;/del&gt; and is now spreading within communities with no link to recent foreign trips . It is no longer crucially tied to foreign sources . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nevertheless , some governments are enacting border closures in an effort to prevent further infiltration . Among those are Canada&amp;rsquo ; s allies : Denmark , Germany and the United States . Others have partial bans or have instituted procedures whereby visitors must &amp;ldquo ; self-isolate&amp;rdquo ; upon return to their homelands . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;18046;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18088;TOOLONG ... new COVID-19 cases in Ottawa Tuesday morning , as province declares **30;18123;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18155;TOOLONG ... State of emergency in Ontario , latest news and other **33;18190;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18225;TOOLONG ... closes all restaurants and bars ; Trudeau closes borders to most **33;18260;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Trudeau government announced Monday that Canada is barring entry to all travellers who are not Canadian citizens , permanent residents or Americans , as well as Canadians who are symptomatic with COVID-19 . ( The Canadian Civil Liberties Association has already said that barring Canadians from flights home because they exhibit symptoms effectively strips them of their right to re-enter the country and may in fact be unconstitutional. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many were surprised by the U.S. exemption . After all , it is not as if COVID-19 only affects certain &amp;ldquo ; ethnicities&amp;rdquo ; and nationalities . Besides , in light of the aforementioned ham-handed initial response by the Trump administration , which incredulously said COVID-19 was a &amp;ldquo ; Democratic Party hoax , &amp;rdquo ; would it not make sense to shut the doors on our American neighbours as well ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yes and no . Yes , because if we are going to &amp;ldquo ; self-isolate&amp;rdquo ; as a nation , it should be complete self-isolation : no exceptions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No , for several very good reasons : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First , we have a VERY long border with the U.S. and it would be simply impossible to bar the frontier entirely ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Second , our economy is inextricably tied to that of the U.S. and shutting the door would have a catastrophic effect on an economy already reeling . Perhaps we could limit cross-border flows to those who play a critical role in bilateral trade , although it is a valid question whether anyone in his or her right mind is thinking of taking a vacation to the Great White North in these challenging times anyway . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Third , perhaps most importantly , border shutdowns feed a disturbing xenophobic and anti-immigrant fringe that is unfortunately present in Canada and other Western nations . These extremists already hate newcomers , particularly if they are Muslim , and display alarming levels of anti-Semitism . A decision to deny all entries from abroad will feed these individuals and give them a sense of victory and emboldenment . Online forums are rife with hate and intolerance towards &amp;ldquo ; The Other . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Everyone in a position of credible authority has been saying that things will get worse before they get better . As a consequence , governments will have to be nimble in their strategies as more information comes in , allowing for better decisions based on science and fact , not fear . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Travel bans are partly based on fear . While they are understandable to an extent , they have to be implemented carefully so they do not give the haters more fodder for their despicable views . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **28;18295;TOOLONG Gurski&lt;/strong&gt; is a retired senior strategic terrorism analyst at CSIS and the Director of the Security Program at the University of Ottawa . **25;18325;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN CITIZEN OPINIONS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;18352;TOOLONG ... letters : COVID-19 -- silver linings , airport germs , greetings and caring&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;18387;TOOLONG ... High-tech giants should have enough cash to withstand the COVID-19 stormhttp : **35;18504;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;18541;TOOLONG ... title= " Kinaxis HQ in Kanata . Jim Bagnall photo " alt= " Kinaxis HQ in Kanata . Jim Bagnall photo " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;18577;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1048909 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We&amp;rsquo ; ve been here before . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2001 during the telecom bust . In 2008-09 in the midst of the great recession . Periods when the capital region&amp;rsquo ; s high-tech engine simply seized up . Orders for software , telecom gear and professional services disappeared , wrecking balance sheets overnight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the years following 2001 , dozens of Ottawa startups &amp;mdash ; from Innovance Networks to Sedona Networks &amp;mdash ; failed for want of investment equity and customers . A decade ago , the near collapse of the international banking sector pushed cash-hungry tech firms over the edge . One of them was Nortel Networks , Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s largest private-sector employer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This time the trigger for what is almost certain to be another economic recession is &lt;a href= " https : **33;18607;TOOLONG ... , a virus without a vaccine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is too early of course to confidently forecast how the sudden imposition of social distancing will affect the economy in the months ahead . The Royal Bank of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s economics group took a stab with its recent prediction that Canada&amp;rsquo ; s economy will shrink at an annual rate of 2.5 per cent after inflation from April 1 to June 30 . Locally , we can take a bit of comfort in the generally healthy state of Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s high-tech pillars as we enter this dark valley . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;18642;TOOLONG : &lt;a href= " https : **33;18677;TOOLONG ... COVID-19 case confirmed at Ciena , Kanata shutdown extended&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Consider the software giants : Shopify , the e-commerce enabler whose software underpins online storefronts for more than one million merchants worldwide , and Kinaxis , the Kanata firm that sells software to multinationals anxious to track their convoluted supply chains . Shopify employs about 1,000 locally while the tally at Kinaxis is 400 workers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;18712;TOOLONG ... title= " Shopify headquarters on Elgin Street in Ottawa . " alt= " Shopify headquarters on Elgin Street in Ottawa . " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;18748;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1577138 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A decade ago , both were relatively tiny . But in the past few years they have transformed into significant operations flush with cash . Shopify at the end of December had a cash mountain of $2.5 billion ( all figures U.S. ) while Kinaxis had $213 million on hand . For companies that last year generated revenues of $1.6 billion and $192 million respectively , that should be plenty to withstand a short-term storm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The same is true of Ciena , the optical products firm that closed its Kanata campus on March 11 after learning one of its 1,750 employees tested positive for the COVID-19 virus . Although Ciena has a relatively thin net cash position of $200 million , this consists of $1 billion cash offset by long-term debts , providing plenty of short-term liquidity . The firm is also coming off a strong fiscal 2019 in which revenues jumped 15 per cent to $3.6 billion and earnings surged . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The software companies reached their relatively safe states using different strategies . Shopify raised cash by selling treasury shares on the stock market , while Kinaxis built a profitable operation that accumulated cash . Ciena took the more difficult route of buying Nortel&amp;rsquo ; s optical products division out of bankruptcy in 2010 , then devoting half a decade to making sure the combined operation meshed . It was expensive and messy but the result was a sizeable global corporation that is stealing market share from its rivals . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All three firms are now faced with the likelihood of having to dip into their savings . For its part , Shopify is pursuing a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to make its e-commerce software the platform of choice for entrepreneurs around the globe . Spending on R&amp;amp ; D , marketing , hiring and new offices will mean quarterly losses for some time to come . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And this was before COVID-19 came along . Although Shopify is riding a growing wave of e-commerce &amp;mdash ; which seems ideally suited for a post COVID-19 world &amp;mdash ; the company still faces a big risk . That&amp;rsquo ; s because an ever growing percentage of Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s revenues depends on how well its online merchants are doing . A general economic recession will hurt their revenues , meaning less for Shopify. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Look at it this way . Shopify depends on two streams of revenues . One comes from merchants who pay a monthly fee for using its software platform &amp;mdash ; a stream that will likely remain fairly steady . The second group of revenues is the one that has been growing fastest , but it&amp;rsquo ; s also the most variable . Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s most recent quarter generated nearly 64 per cent of its revenues through applications &amp;mdash ; shipping , payment systems , inventory analysis , you name it . The deeper the economic recession , the faster these revenues will shrink . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And there&amp;rsquo ; s a secondary risk embedded here because Shopify has been lending money to its online customers through its Shopify Capital program . The latter aims to help entrepreneurs smooth out their cash flow while they build their businesses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If more of our merchants cease operations , experience a decline in their sales , or engage in fraudulent behaviour , &amp;rdquo ; Shopify warned in its yearend financial filing , &amp;ldquo ; it would make it more difficult for us to obtain the receivables we have purchased via merchant cash advances or to obtain repayment of loans we have made&amp;rdquo ; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Because Shopify has yet to experience an economic downturn it lacks a solid understanding of how all these factors will play out , and how quickly . Which only reinforces the wisdom of its multi-year strategy of raising money from the stock markets while the latter were strong . The last time Shopify sold shares , during the third quarter of 2019 , the company charged $317.50 per share to raise nearly $700 million . That&amp;rsquo ; s actually not far off the low price on Monday , though it&amp;rsquo ; s highly unlikely any publicly traded firm would be able to sell treasury shares until the stock markets calm down . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kinaxis , unlike Shopify , has built most of its financial stability on the rock of profits . It also depends on far fewer , much larger customers &amp;mdash ; such as Ford Motor , Nissan , Celestica and First Solar &amp;mdash ; with which it has deep relations and multi-year contracts . This suggests that if the COVID-19 downturn is short , the majority of Kinaxis&amp;rsquo ; s revenues should be relatively unaffected . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Unknown is how many new customer contracts Kinaxis might have been on the verge of winning but which will now be delayed as potential clients hit the pause button . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Similar considerations apply to Ciena&amp;rsquo ; s order book . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What we do know is that these three tech giants are at least entering the post COVID-19 world from a position of strength . And that could make all the difference in the months ahead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whether that will also be true of the region&amp;rsquo ; s cash-hungry tech startups is another story . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;18778;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18820;TOOLONG ... least 40 per cent of Americans will become infected by coronavirus , and then the grim choices **26;18855;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18883;TOOLONG ... definition a temporary shock : ' Canadian economy likely set for sharp rebound , despite current **26;18918;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18946;TOOLONG ... medical officer recommends all restaurants and bars close ; Trudeau closes borders to most **33;18981;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; James BagnallTue , 17 Mar 2020 14:52:11 **45;19016;TOOLONG ... These figures prompted plans for 750,000 hospital beds and a stockpile of one million coffins ; more than 30 million gas masks were issued and air raid shelters issued . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " xMsoNormal " &gt;While I recall no signs of panic at that time , a great sense of community spirit did occur ; normally reserved neighbours came together and official directions were closely followed without complaint . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " xMsoNormal " &gt;In regard to hoarding , there was very little , if any , although I was involved in one minor incident . Our jails are a petri dish for the rapid spread of coronavirus . Let 's release non-violent inmateshttp : **33;19568;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19603;TOOLONG ... title= " Barbed wire tops the fences of the Ottawa Carleton Detention Centre . It 's impossible to practise ' social distancing ' when you 're in jail . " alt= " Barbed wire tops the fences of the Ottawa Carleton Detention Centre . It 's impossible to practise ' social distancing ' when you 're in jail . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19639;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1580765 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s jails , including the notorious Innes Road detention centre in Ottawa , are filthy , overcrowded , and populated by some of our community&amp;rsquo ; s most vulnerable people . In other words , they are a perfect petri dish for the spread of the novel coronavirus. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our jails are not Dickensian hellholes by accident , they are that way by design . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last December , in a damning decision , the Ontario Superior Court ruled that conditions at the Toronto South Detention Centre were &amp;ldquo ; inhumane and fail to comport with basic standards of human decency. &amp;rdquo ; Inmates were often confined to crowded small cells for as long as seven days , without access to showers . Clothing and bedding were often stained with urine , feces or blood , and there were bedbug infestations and other unsanitary conditions that led to untreatable infections . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The court ruled that those horrendous conditions were a &amp;ldquo ; deliberate policy choice to treat offenders in an inhumane fashion &amp;hellip ; rather than devote appropriate resources to the operation of the institution . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And that same neglect and absence of basic human decency has set the conditions for COVID-19 to sweep through our jails like a firestorm. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You see , behind bars there can be no &amp;ldquo ; social distancing . &amp;rdquo ; The majority of Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s jails are filled to more than 80 per cent above their planned capacity . The Ottawa-Carleton Detention Centre ( OCDC ) currently has a 518-bed capacity &amp;ndash ; 178 per cent higher than its original 186-bed limit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The government&amp;rsquo ; s solution to overcrowding has been to shoehorn three inmates into a cell built for two . In some cases , up to four inmates are held in a 40-sq. -ft. cell designed for two people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The combination of unsanitary conditions , overcrowding , poor medical care and a vulnerable population is a perfect storm for infection . Last month , it only took days for a gastrointestinal virus to sweep through the population at OCDC. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is inevitable that COVID-19 will do the same . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And until very recently , the government did not seem to have much of a plan . As late as last Thursday , guards at OCDC told me that no one had told them about any special procedures or contingencies . It was business as usual . And the usual business is unsanitary and overcrowded conditions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since then , the government has announced that inmates serving weekend sentences will be given temporary absence passes and will be permitted to return to their homes . This is a good , although very late , first step . But more needs to be done to prevent our jails from becoming at best sick houses and at worst morgues. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The only real solution is depopulation . The government must immediately release every non-violent inmate . This means bail for those accused of non-violent crimes and temporary absence permits for individuals serving sentences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is not a soft-on-crime measure ; it is a necessary , lifesaving response . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Depopulating jails is the humane and responsible action in the face of a national public health emergency . The alternative is a reservoir of death and infection that will inevitably spread and prolong the epidemic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We must act now because a catastrophe in our jails will also worsen COVID-19&amp;rsquo ; s impact on the rest of the justice system . Ontario courts have already : suspended jury trials ; cancelled small claims hearings ; and as of Monday , cancelled all criminal trials and appearances for out-of-custody accused for the next 10 weeks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is a brief window to get this right and we are in all likelihood heading towards some chaos at the courthouse . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; An outbreak of COVID-19 at the jails will only make the courthouse chaos worse . If jails become a hotspot for infections and prolonged quarantines are required , what could have been manageable chaos will become an extended and unworkable quagmire that could last well into next year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Inmates that I have spoken with are terrified . They are scared they will be infected . They are scared they will not receive treatment . They are scared that they will suffer and die alone . They are terrified that they will be forgotten . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And they are right , because before COVID-19 , the government was blissfully indifferent to the inhumane conditions at its jails . And now it seems totally unprepared . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No one truly knows a nation until one has been inside its jails . Right now , the inside of our jails is a dangerous and infectious disgrace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **31;19669;TOOLONG Spratt&lt;/strong&gt; is a partner at the Ottawa criminal law firm Abergel Goldstein &amp; Partners and co-host of the legal and political podcast The Docket . Confirmed cases , latest news and other developments in Ottawa&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Michael SprattMon , 16 Mar 2020 17:31:40 **45;19807;TOOLONG ... We can turn the COVID-19 lemon into social lemonadehttp : **32;19854;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19888;TOOLONG ... title= " You ca n't socialize in person , but you can still reach out in many , many ways . " alt= " You ca n't socialize in person , but you can still reach out in many , many ways . " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;19924;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1580825 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Undoubtedly , many of us would be willing to give up almost every material thing to have the COVID-19 virus disappear . But that is not on the option list . Quarantine , self-isolation , social distancing , school closings , working at home : these are the words we are hearing . These words will not be going away any time soon . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fortunately , the classic advice that &amp;ldquo ; when life serves you lemons , make lemonade , &amp;rdquo ; still applies , even though we have all been presented with mega doses of lemons . This is not to minimize the herculean issues we face , just to accentuate the opportunities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I have always believed that people are fundamentally good , but that life sometimes gets in the way . Perhaps the greatest intrusion on our ability to be kind is time . When we are in a rush to get somewhere , usually work or an event , we might cut people off on the road . We are so focused on getting there that we allow nothing to slow us down or get in the way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a hurry , we are less likely to hold doors open , or hold the elevator for those rushing to get in . These are small gestures that loom large for those who benefit from them . We do not purposefully decide to be mean or oblivious . We are just in a hurry . But if we have the time , or make a conscious effort to create the time , we will yield more often , hold doors open more often , and generally be even more kind and nice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With all the lemons that seem to be piling up daily , one thing that we all will have more of is &amp;ndash ; time . No hockey to watch , no basketball to watch , no golf to watch ( except maybe re-runs ) , for the foreseeable future . Working at home chops so much driving time , making more time available . Schools closing likewise creates time , surely for the students . In fact , we may have too much time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What will we do with all this time ? Will we see it as a curse , or as a gift ? This most unwelcome COVID-19 intrusion on our lives does contain not a small amount of lemonade potential . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Permit me to share a few ideas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We are used to handshakes , embraces , hugs . All this is now suspended . We are in social distancing mode . Why not transmute social distancing into societal concern , as a way to fill the vacuum created by social distancing . With time on our hands , we can contact family and friends with whom heretofore we did not have as much communication as we would have liked . Telephone , FaceTime and so on , all become golden opportunities that beckon &amp;ndash ; a great lemonade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With the gift of time , we can look for ways to volunteer to help in these challenging times . It could be through organizations , or through calling those who are alone to ask if they need anything , and proceeding to fill that need . More lemonade . The media stories of such magnificent gestures are heartwarming and inspiring . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We realize that we are all in this together , and the more emotionally we are together , the better are our chances that we as a society will overcome this pandemic and its adverse affects . In effect , any self-transcending decision we make for the greater good of everyone becomes more than just nice . Now , such actions are potentially life-saving . Yes , we all now have the opportunity , indeed the imperative , to be life-savers . Even more lemonade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A decision to stay home , rather than travel for a long planned pleasure trip , is a life-saving gesture . A decision to shop late at night when it is less crowded is not only prudent ; it is potentially life-saving . Judicious purchasing so that others also will have an adequate supply of basic food and sanitary needs is life-saving . Terrific lemonade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hatchet burying is also an endeavour we can employ . In light of the present enveloping crisis , whatever dispute we may have with someone , family or former friend , becomes even more trivial . So , with time on our hands , what a great opportunity to stretch out a &amp;ldquo ; hand&amp;rdquo ; in friendship and reconciliation . Potent lemonade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Being &amp;ldquo ; locked up&amp;rdquo ; at home , whether as a result of mandatory quarantine or self isolation , or as a result of closures , can be quite difficult . It is easier said than done , but if we saw this as a golden opportunity to create emotional connectedness when previously there was no time for it , that would be sweet lemonade . &amp;nbsp ; Spousal relationships , parent-child relationships , sibling relationships &amp;ndash ; all these we will now have the time to hopefully make better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; More available time also makes more possible the realization of projects or personal goals that were on hold , such as reading or writing . A more personal lemonade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I fervently hope and pray that we will soon overcome this most serious assault on our collective well being . Simultaneously , I fervently wish that we will use the newly available time and opportunity to enhance our immediate and personal world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **29;19954;TOOLONG Dr. Reuven P. You , too , can homeschool the kids during the COVID-19 crisishttp : **34;20137;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20173;TOOLONG ... title= " Teaching your own child : How hard can this be ? " alt= " Teaching your own child : How hard can this be ? " data-portal-copyright= " monkeybusinessimages " **28;20209;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1580446 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; With the medical officer of health telling us all bluntly to stay home , does the prospect of playing substitute teacher for your kids for the next few weeks make you anxious ? I&amp;rsquo ; m here to reassure you . You won&amp;rsquo ; t find it easy , but you&amp;rsquo ; ll do a fine job . Everything is going to be OK. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I spent 12 years glued to my three children , homeschooling since the first one was born in 2006 until the youngest started attending public school in 2018 , all the while working from home as a freelancer . With your formal &amp;ldquo ; March Break&amp;rdquo ; over and they need to start learning again , a few weeks is nothing . You can do this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first rule is : Manage your expectations . Even if your employer is supporting you working from home , you still have to work , so it&amp;rsquo ; s important for you and your kids to understand that little thing called &amp;ldquo ; the art of the possible . &amp;rdquo ; Have a frank and open discussion with them about it , tell them what you expect and let them express themselves too . Your home should be a safe space . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ask them to be patient &amp;ndash ; and try to exhibit that fine quality yourself . You&amp;rsquo ; re bound to fail . That&amp;rsquo ; s OK , as long as you keep trying . Above all else , promise each other to keep the dialogue open , and to make changes to your plans if and when necessary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My golden rule is to put my relationship with my children before the curriculum . Yes , math is important . But it&amp;rsquo ; s not worth World War III with a seven-year-old you otherwise love beyond words . Know when to step back . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , how do you organize your day ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Start with a deep breath . If you manage two hours of schooling per day , you&amp;rsquo ; ll be doing great . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;20239;TOOLONG : &lt;a href= " https : **33;20274;TOOLONG ... to home-school during a pandemic ? We talked to an Ottawa parent who 's done it for years&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In my experience , morning is the best time for learning . If you can devote 45 to 60 minutes to sit with them and go over lessons , that&amp;rsquo ; s the time to do it . Then they should spend another 30 to 45 minutes doing exercises based on the lessons you just went over , or any other exercise you deem suitable . Many teachers have sent lesson plans home with the kids . If yours did that , use it as a guide . If you didn&amp;rsquo ; t get anything , use the resources below . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By all means let your kids see you struggle to come up with good lessons for them . They&amp;rsquo ; ll get a brand-new appreciation for how much work goes into their education and how much you love them and care about their wellbeing . These are brownie points worth collecting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Review their exercises with them . But don&amp;rsquo ; t grade ! Congratulate them on what they got right , and explain that anything they had trouble with will be reviewed the next day . Focus on building their abilities , and give as much praise as possible . Always&amp;nbsp ; be proud of their efforts . Keep in mind this whole situation is hard for them , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The rest of the morning should be off . Free time is a beautiful educational tool . But no screens . They should be playing , or reading , or drawing , or just lying on the couch daydreaming until lunch . If they fight , make them clean the bathroom . Guaranteed harmony , or a sparkling en-suite &amp;mdash ; either one feels like victory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During lunch , discuss topics they&amp;rsquo ; re curious about . It can be anything , including the science of farts . After lunch , install them in front of the Google machine and make them research something that intrigues them so they can teach&amp;nbsp ; you&amp;nbsp ; what they discovered at dinner . Kids love showing off how much they know . Be a good student and listen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Around 2 p.m. , send them to read a novel or watch a movie . Not a TV show ; a feature-length movie . I don&amp;rsquo ; t care what the movie is about , provided it&amp;rsquo ; s long enough to have a narrative arc and character development . Stories are a wonderful and tragically underrated educational tool . At 3:30 p.m. , they should be free to do whatever they normally do when they come home from school . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s it . Oh , and if you don&amp;rsquo ; t get everything done , that&amp;rsquo ; s OK . Take another deep breath . Your kids are watching how you react to difficult circumstances . Nobody is expected to get everything right the first time , but we must all do our best . Remember : you&amp;rsquo ; re teaching them that lesson , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Good luck . Coping with coronavirus -- Stay calm , listen to public **27;20677;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; Brigitte PellerinMon , 16 Mar 2020 11:58:12 **45;20706;TOOLONG ... Autistic children in Ontario deserve a better interim planhttp : **36;20753;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20791;TOOLONG ... title= " Jack Monaghan , six , and Charlotte Monaghan , four , need different levels of autism support services . " alt= " Jack Monaghan , six , and Charlotte Monaghan , four , need different levels of autism support services . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20827;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1578089 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As a parent of two autistic children , I&amp;rsquo ; m used to being told I have to wait . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You wait for a diagnosis , sometimes months or even years . Then , you wait in line for therapy . You&amp;rsquo ; re told there is a program that could help your children learn in their own unique ways , with one-on-one specialized support to gain necessary skills in self-help , communication and independence . Strategies could be developed to help keep them safe from the dangers they don&amp;rsquo ; t often perceive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The problem is that this level of support is financially unreachable for most families if paid for privately , especially with a high-needs child such as my son , with therapy costs of more than $80,000 a year . That&amp;rsquo ; s why government programs such as the Ontario Autism Program ( OAP ) are supposed to exist &amp;ndash ; to make help available to those who need it . Since there are nearly 40,000 other autistic children in Ontario , all looking for support , you&amp;rsquo ; re told you have to wait . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now imagine you&amp;rsquo ; ve been waiting on that list for two or more years , and you&amp;rsquo ; re told that what you were waiting for , the program that would give your child help based on their individual needs , is gone . The government blew it up . The new plan would arbitrarily give payments to kids based solely on their age , spread so thinly that few children would have enough funding to actually get meaningful support . This is what my daughter faces now . Her needs may be less than her brother&amp;rsquo ; s , but individual needs are not even being considered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Families were devastated . Outraged . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But families stood up , fighting to give their kids the support they need and deserve . After months of protests , it looked like things might change . An advisory panel was assembled , which worked through the summer to put together a thorough list of recommendations on how to fix the program . We were assured the new program was going to be ready in April 2020 . We just had to wait a little longer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then families were dealt another devastating blow , just days before Christmas , and informed that the program might not be ready until 2021 . It was heartbreaking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So what can the government do in the interim ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The need for a bridging program is not a new concept . The Liberal government faced a similar dilemma in 2016/17 when it announced its changes to the autism program , and needed a way to support families who were caught in the middle . Renewable direct funding payments were made available to this cohort of families . The reason it was so effective was that it gave the eligible kids access to exactly the amount of support they required as recommended by their therapists . Not more . Not less . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The current government could learn from this , and make a similar program available to a large number of children . The biggest complaint about the interim autism program right now is that it&amp;rsquo ; s not based on need . Offering renewable interim payments could allow many children the opportunity to obtain needs-based therapy immediately . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With a promised $600-million budget , there&amp;rsquo ; s plenty of money available ; it just needs to be released . Do kids in the old program deserve a better quality of care than everyone else ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We recently learned that the government spent just half of the OAP budget in the first three quarters of the current fiscal year . While families desperately waited for support , the money was there but , inexplicably , held back . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Families of autistic children want a program that can give their kids the tools they need to succeed in life . Until a true needs-based program is ready , the government should make every effort to learn from their mistakes , set their pride aside , and make needs-based therapy a reality today . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Families have waited long enough . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **31;20857;TOOLONG Monaghan&lt;/strong&gt; is an optometrist in Ottawa , and a father to two children with autism : a son with high needs , and a daughter with mild needs . @drpmonaghan&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;20890;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;21632;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1579543 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Self-isolation . Flattening the curve . Social distancing . All phrases Canadians weren&amp;rsquo ; t using a few months ago . All phrases we&amp;rsquo ; re now tossing around as if they&amp;rsquo ; ve always been part of our collective vocabulary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That most people know what they mean is encouraging in the time of COVID-19 , a.k.a. the novel coronavirus . Canadians are paying close attention to the advice of experts . We trust the science to guide our health-care policies . Trust between citizens and experts will be vital if we are to limit the impact of the virus . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So let&amp;rsquo ; s start with some advice to public health experts and providers at all levels : Be as transparent and as timely as possible with information . In an over-burdened health care eco-system , there will be a temptation to focus on the immediate crisis and save the explaining for later . The public needs both . So far , our governments have made genuine efforts at openness . Bravo . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But err on the side of even fuller disclosure . In Ottawa earlier this week , local officials left the impression that the first diagnosed patient here had not gone to work after returning from abroad ; in fact , he had . If there are shortages of equipment , ventilators or staff , tell the public . And keep explaining . Ottawa has had recent experience with what happens to public trust&amp;nbsp ; &amp;ndash ; we refer to LRT &amp;ndash ; when information is incomplete or withheld . Try to take more than &amp;ldquo ; one question per media outlet&amp;rdquo ; at press conferences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Correct any mistakes or wrong advice promptly . The premier suggested earlier this week that families keep their March break travel plans . That was bad advice . There will be more bad advice , and occasional missteps . We all understand that . Science may change ; diagnosis and treatment may need to update ; spokespeople may just be fatigued . Correct the record promptly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , advice to the public : Hysteria , too , can be contagious . Sure , it&amp;rsquo ; s difficult to find hand sanitizer , but last time we checked , there was lots of soap for sale . Purchase and use it . Long lineups in grocery stores have been orderly , but are mostly unnecessary . Buy what you need ; don&amp;rsquo ; t hoard . Follow the guidance of public health . And don&amp;rsquo ; t spread unsubstantiated social media bilge. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you know someone who is in &amp;ldquo ; self-isolation&amp;rdquo ; &amp;ndash ; the number will jump now that public health advises staying home if you&amp;rsquo ; ve just returned from abroad &amp;ndash ; ask if you can help . Older or frail people in particular might appreciate knowing that someone will deliver their groceries or take care of their green bin . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Challenging times lie ahead . Coronavirus shows the urgent need to invest in health infrastructurehttp : **26;22330;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;22358;TOOLONG ... title= " Three prairie farmers wear masks to ward off the Spanish flu that killed thousands in 1918. " alt= " Three prairie farmers wear masks to ward off the Spanish flu that killed thousands in 1918. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;22394;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1578291 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bill Gates recently speculated that COVID-19 could be the &amp;ldquo ; once in a century&amp;rdquo ; disease whose severity rivals that of the 1918 Spanish Flu . That disease was so dire that it likely played a role in ending the First World War , having removed so many soldiers from the battlefield. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; COVID-19 has already caused profound economic , psychological and even climatic impacts . But with a century of experience since the Spanish Flu , how resilient is our health infrastructure against this and future pandemics ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The &lt;a href= " https : //www.ghsindex.org/ " &gt;2019 Global Health Security Index&lt;/a&gt; ranked 195 countries according to their abilities to prevent , detect and respond to biological threats . Overall , the world scored a disappointing 40.2 out of a possible 100 points , with the United States ranking as the most secure nation with a score of 83 , and Canada ranking a respectable fifth with 75.3 points . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada&amp;rsquo ; s comparatively high score is based mostly on our detection capability , due in large part to our excellent laboratory facilities and well-trained workforce , both of which received perfect scores . Our ability to respond to an existing epidemic , though , was not as well rated , at 60.7. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The capacity to respond is a systems management issue . During a pandemic , a nation needs a robust health care system that can treat people at scale and quickly isolate carriers . With international coordination , we also need an integrated biopharmaceuticals industry that can rapidly develop , test , manufacture and deploy vaccines and treatments . And this all hangs upon a communications infrastructure for information dissemination and the assuagement of panic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We should be investing more in disease surveillance . Knowing when and where new cases of diseases occur can inexpensively guide resource allocation . In the era of digital communication and data capacity , getting accurate , real-time information on incident cases should not be as challenging as it is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And yet , globally , surveillance is fundamentally weak , with many countries having trivial capacity to identify outbreaks . In Canada , though , scores of diseases are monitored by dedicated surveillance programs . We have a good grasp of our influenza burden , for example , because of our national flu &amp;nbsp ; surveillance system , &lt;a href= " https : **33;22424;TOOLONG ... . The inclusion of COVID-19 in this paradigm would help us track and manage that disease&amp;rsquo ; s spread . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Related data tools help to draw relationships between clusters of cases , making instances of &amp;ldquo ; community transmission&amp;rdquo ; less mysterious . Absent such tools , cases can appear to manifest without a clear transmission route , fomenting panic and confounding containment efforts . Canada has world-class expertise in such analytics . We need the resources and leadership to deploy that capability onto the field at scale . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;22459;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;22501;TOOLONG ... minutes that changed our world : How COVID-19 went from abstract to very real in a **26;22536;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;22564;TOOLONG ... can kill me . ' For transplant patients , shortage of hand sanitizer a matter of life and **26;22599;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;22627;TOOLONG ... COVID-19 testing could also reduce spread in Canada : **35;22662;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;22699;TOOLONG ... Social distancing is the key for the next phase of **29;22734;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Scale is the magic word for pandemic response . All nations&amp;rsquo ; outbreak plans assume relatively low numbers of cases . But if hospitals become overwhelmed , how do we distribute care at a national level ? And do we have the legislative power , ethical oversight and political cover to enact more restrictive isolation policies , should that need arise ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The one preparedness category in which Canada received a score of zero was in our failure to exercise our response plans . In the wake of SARS , much thought went into building our Maginot Line against the next viral assault . Yet that bulwark remained truly untested until now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So even if COVID-19 is not the &amp;ldquo ; once in a century&amp;rdquo ; disease Bill Gates warned us about , we can nevertheless consider it a working test of our pandemic resilience systems , which will no doubt be challenged repeatedly and at greater intensities in decades to come . We can choose to invest in the appropriate infrastructure to keep Canadians safe from pandemic disease , now and in the future . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **26;22765;TOOLONG . " data-portal-copyright= " Adrian Wyld " **28;22952;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1578327 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the span of less than 24 hours , the United States imposed an incoming travel &amp;nbsp ; ban on continental Europe , the NBA and NHL suspended their seasons and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau went into self-isolation . This rapidly escalating situation has not only redefined &amp;ldquo ; cancel culture&amp;rdquo ; as we know it , but it has brought into clear focus the magnitude of the public health crisis that Ontario is about to face . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If we hope to learn from the experiences of China , South Korea , Iran and Italy , we need to act decisively in order to ready ourselves for a pandemic that has the potential to rapidly overwhelm our health care system . This is especially true as we move from a containment to a delay phase for COVID-19 in a crucial attempt to flatten the curve on a virus 10 times more deadly than the flu . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This type of language may seem alarmist , but medical experts agree that being over-prepared for this problem would be a best-case scenario . The risk of community spread , acceleration of the number of cases as we scale up testing , and the rising hospitalization and death rates will soon become a reality , much like in other countries , including the United States . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What this means is that we need to be very serious about next steps . From a public health viewpoint , this means educating communities about diligent hand-washing , limiting hand-shaking , covering coughs and sneezes , limiting the touching of one&amp;rsquo ; s face and staying home from work when you&amp;rsquo ; re sick . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In order to help stop the spread of COVID-19 in our communities , however , one of the most important tools we have is social distancing . By definition , this means staying at least three feet from anyone who is coughing or sneezing , but its applications should be broadened . We are seeing this happen on a larger scale with the cancelling of university classes , sporting events , parades , concerts and other large gatherings here and around the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a dangerous lack of judgment , Premier Doug Ford Thursday actually encouraged Ontarians to travel for March Break . This might be the worst advice to give during a global pandemic . In fact , he should have advised the opposite : all non-essential travel should be cancelled immediately . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indeed , one of the exacerbating features of the COVID-19 spread in China was travel associated with New Year celebrations . By encouraging travel , not only does Ford increase our risk at home but he recklessly threatens the public health systems of countries that may not have the resources to cope with an outbreak potentially exported by Ontarians. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are also suggestions that public health authorities , along with different levels of government , have acted too slowly . The WHO only this week declared COVID-19 a pandemic , which likely could have happened weeks before and would have given countries a longer runway to adequately prepare for the seriousness of this disease . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;22982;TOOLONG ... title= " Director-General of the World Health Organization ( WHO ) Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus answers questions of the novel coronavirus. " alt= " Director-General of the World Health Organization ( WHO ) Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus answers questions of the novel coronavirus. " data-portal-copyright= " DENIS BALIBOUSE " **28;23018;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1555242 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The same may be happening here . Which is why , at this point in the COVID-19 lifecycle in Ontario , the collaboration between government , public health and medical officials is key to ensuring the safety of our communities . This means clear and consistent messaging with transparent data-sharing in order to reduce confusion among the public . We have seen positive steps by medical teams including knowledge translation between health-care professionals , onboarding of rapid assessment centres and the expansion of telemedicine infrastructure . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This should dovetail with a responsible government plan , including prompt federal fiscal stimulus for the impending economic burden , tighter screening and isolation protocols for travellers coming from abroad and coordinated regional efforts to distribute personal protective equipment for health care workers . This should also be supported by early procurement and deployment of necessary medical devices such as respirators and ventilators , alongside planning for medical triaging and makeshift ICUs. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Amidst the dizzying evolution of this pandemic in Ontario , let&amp;rsquo ; s recognize that we&amp;rsquo ; re all in this together . Canadian authorities&lt;/a&gt; for their handling of the public response to the crisis .
